events.title: Sarah conceives and bears Isaac to Abraham
events.narrative_summary: The LORD visits Sarah as he had said, and she conceives and bears Abraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time God had spoken of.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 21:5 gives Abraham's age at Isaac's birth as one hundred, so the birth is anchor.isaac_birth with offset 0 (REGNAL_YEAR). Margin 1 year, since an age covers the whole year. The 'appointed time' (21:2) is 'at this time next year' of 18:10, the year after Gen 20 (2067 BCE, Abraham 99). The nine months of pregnancy are not a separate event.
events.ancient_year_marker: At the appointed time, when Abraham was a hundred years old

events.title: Abraham names his newborn son Isaac
events.narrative_summary: Abraham calls the name of the son Sarah bore him Isaac.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word; naming follows the birth. Anchored on the birth's END, offset 0, 10 minutes, margin 1 day (the name may have been given at the circumcision, 7 days later). Tier follows the age that frames the scene (REGNAL_YEAR).

events.title: Abraham circumcises Isaac at eight days old
events.narrative_summary: Abraham circumcises his son Isaac when he is eight days old, as God commanded. The narrator adds that Abraham was a hundred years old when Isaac was born.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'A son of eight days' is the eighth day of life, counted with the birth day as the first: offset 7 days from the birth's START, margin 1 day for the Hebrew-day counting (birth near evening could shift it). DAY_SEQUENCE: days counted.
events.ancient_year_marker: When Abraham was a hundred years old

events.title: Sarah says God has made her laugh
events.narrative_summary: Sarah says God has made laughter for her and everyone who hears will laugh with her. She asks who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children, since she has borne him a son in his old age.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The text gives no time; she speaks of nursing, so after the birth. Placed at the circumcision's END with margin 1 month. Tier follows the framing age (REGNAL_YEAR).

events.title: Abraham holds a great feast when Isaac is weaned
events.narrative_summary: The child grows and is weaned, and Abraham makes a great feast on the day Isaac is weaned.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No age is given. Offset 2 years from the birth's START (the usual nursing span; 1 Sam 1:22–24 per Rashbam; 2 Macc 7:27 says three), margin 1 year. Duration 1 day for the feast. REGNAL_YEAR since it falls under the framing age and has no finer time word.

events.title: Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and demands his expulsion
events.narrative_summary: Sarah sees the son of Hagar the Egyptian mocking and tells Abraham to drive out the slave woman and her son, who must not inherit with Isaac. The matter is very grievous to Abraham because of his son.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Undated in the text; placed on the day of the feast, 3 hours after its start, with margin 7 days. Tier REGNAL_YEAR, because no time word is given and the scene falls under the framing age.

events.title: God tells Abraham to listen to Sarah and promises Ishmael a nation
events.narrative_summary: God tells Abraham not to be grieved about the boy and the slave woman, to heed all Sarah says, because Isaac's line will carry his name. God will also make a nation of the slave woman's son because he is Abraham's seed.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows Abraham's distress directly; the next verse has Abraham rising early in the morning, so this is the night before. Anchored on the demand's END, 10 minutes, margin 12 hours. REGNAL_YEAR (no time word of its own).

events.title: Abraham rises early and sends Hagar and Ishmael away
events.narrative_summary: Abraham rises early in the morning, gives Hagar bread and a skin of water on her shoulder together with the boy, and sends her away. She goes and wanders in the wilderness of Beer-sheba.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Rose early in the morning': BOKER after the preceding night, anchored on the speech's END. DIURNAL_HOUR; margin 2 hours.

events.title: The water runs out and Hagar sets Ishmael under a bush
events.narrative_summary: The water in the skin is spent. Hagar casts the boy under one of the bushes, sits down a bowshot away so as not to see him die, and weeps aloud.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The text gives no time; a skin of water for two people in desert heat lasts about a day. Offset 1 day from the departure's END, margin 1 day. DAY_SEQUENCE, counted in days.

events.title: God hears the boy and shows Hagar a well
events.narrative_summary: God hears the boy's voice, and the angel of God calls to Hagar from heaven: do not fear, lift up the boy, for God will make him a great nation. God opens her eyes to a well of water, and she fills the skin and gives the boy a drink.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediate response to the weeping; no gap in the text. Anchored on the previous event's END, 1 hour, margin 2 hours. DAY_SEQUENCE: same day as the despair.

events.title: Ishmael grows up an archer in Paran and takes an Egyptian wife
events.narrative_summary: God is with the boy; he grows, lives in the wilderness and becomes a bowman. He settles in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother takes him a wife from the land of Egypt.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No figure in the text. A span of about 10 years from the rescue (margin 5 years) is an estimate, hence MACRO_ERA. Paran to Egypt is about 334 km in a straight line; the marriage is not dated separately.

events.title: Abimelech and Phicol ask Abraham to swear fidelity
events.narrative_summary: At that time Abimelech and Phicol, his army commander, tell Abraham that God is with him in all he does. They ask him to swear by God not to deal falsely with them or their descendants, but to show the same loyalty; Abraham agrees to swear.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'At that time' (21:22) is vague: Rashbam links it to Isaac's birth, Radak to the birth or the weaning. Anchored on the birth's START with offset 1 year and margin 18 months, so the span runs from the birth (Rashbam) to about 2.5 years, past the weaning at about 2 years (Radak), and covers both readings. REGNAL_YEAR (the scene falls under Abraham's age at Isaac's birth).

events.title: Abraham reproves Abimelech about the seized well
events.narrative_summary: Abraham reproves Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants seized. Abimelech says he did not know who did it, that Abraham had not told him, and that he heard of it only that day.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Direct continuation of the same conversation: anchored on the proposal's END, 30 minutes, margin 1 hour. REGNAL_YEAR, as the scene has no time word of its own.

events.title: Abraham and Abimelech make a covenant at Beer-sheba
events.narrative_summary: Abraham gives sheep and oxen to Abimelech and they make a covenant. He sets seven ewe lambs apart as a witness that he dug the well, and the place is named Beer-sheba, where both swore. Abimelech and Phicol then return to the land of the Philistines.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous with the talks; anchored on the reproof's END. Duration 3 hours for the gifts, oath, lambs and the departure; margin 1 hour. REGNAL_YEAR. Beer-sheba to Philistia is about 54 km, but the return is not dated.

events.title: Abraham plants a tamarisk and calls on the LORD, the Everlasting God
events.narrative_summary: Abraham plants a tamarisk tree at Beer-sheba and calls there on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: After the covenant; no gap given. Anchored on the covenant's END, 2 hours, margin 1 month (a planting may follow later). REGNAL_YEAR.

events.title: Abraham lives in the land of the Philistines many days
events.narrative_summary: Abraham sojourns in the land of the Philistines for many days.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Many days' (21:34) is vague. Rashi counts 26 years here, one more than Abraham's 25 years at Hebron, ending 12 years before the binding of Isaac. Anchored on the start of the move to Gerar (Gen 20:1), duration 26 years, margin 10 years. MACRO_ERA.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: God commanded that every male be circumcised on the eighth day (17:12), and Abraham circumcises Isaac at eight days as God had commanded (21:4).
God promised Abraham that Sarah would bear Isaac at the set time (17:19, 21), and she bears him at that set time (21:2).
The LORD said he would return at the appointed time and Sarah would have a son (18:10, 14), and 21:1 says he did to Sarah as he had spoken.
Abimelech asks for an oath and Abraham agrees to swear (21:23–24), and they make the covenant (21:27, 32).
Settling the dispute over the seized well leads to the seven lambs given as witness to Abraham's well (21:25–30).
Sent into the wilderness with a skin of water, Hagar runs out of water and despairs (21:14–15).
God tells Abraham to listen to Sarah (21:12), and Abraham rises early the next morning to send Hagar away (21:14).
God hears the boy's voice as he lies dying and answers by calling to Hagar and showing her a well (21:16–17).
Abraham's distress at Sarah's demand about his son (21:11) leads God to speak to him (21:12).

entities.etymology_meaning: The word for 'seven' (sheva') is tied in the text to the name Beer-sheba.
entities.summary_bio: Seven lambs from Abraham's flock that he sets apart and gives to Abimelech. By accepting them Abimelech is a witness that Abraham dug the well.
A tree Abraham plants at Beer-sheba. There he calls on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Well of water'; the text gives it no proper name.
entities.summary_bio: A well that God shows Hagar after opening her eyes. She fills the skin and gives the boy water to drink.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'place of caverns' or 'abundant in foliage'; the meaning is uncertain.
entities.summary_bio: A desert region south of Canaan in the Sinai and Negev area. Ishmael settles there as an archer after he and his mother are sent away, and his mother takes him a wife from the land of Egypt.

entities.etymology_meaning: Beer-sheba is explained as 'well of the oath' or 'well of seven', from the oath and the seven lambs (vv. 28–31).
entities.summary_bio: The well that Abimelech's servants seized and Abraham confirms as his own by giving seven ewe lambs as witness. It gives the place its name.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Wilderness of the well of the oath' or 'of the seven'; the name Beer-sheba is explained later in the chapter (v. 31).
entities.summary_bio: The dry country in which Hagar wanders after Abraham sends her away with bread and water. The skin of water runs out here and Ishmael is laid under a bush.
An Egyptian woman whom Hagar takes as a wife for Ishmael after he settles in the wilderness of Paran. Hagar's own origin explains the choice.

components.evidence_explanation: Gen 21:27 and 21:32: the two men made a covenant at Beer-sheba.
Gen 21:4 says Abraham circumcised Isaac at eight days old as God commanded.
Gen 21:15–16: the water is gone and Hagar sets the boy down so as not to see him die.

components.label_value: Living in the wilderness of Paran
components.evidence_explanation: Gen 21:21 says he lived in the wilderness of Paran.
Gen 21:20 says he became an archer.
Gen 21:21: his mother took him a wife from the land of Egypt.
Gen 21:2 says Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age.

systems.name: Disinheritance by expulsion
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Law collections from Mesopotamia treat a concubine's or slave woman's son as an heir only if the father acknowledges him, and the household could dismiss a slave woman and her child; freeing them was sometimes required.
rules_and_mechanics: The wife demands that the slave woman and her son be driven out so the son of the wife is the only heir.
The father may resist, but here God tells him to comply.
The expelled receive provisions for the way but no share of the estate.

systems.name: The LORD visits a barren woman
systems.ancient_near_east_context: In the ancient Near East a woman's fertility was widely seen as the gift of a god; the Hebrew verb 'visit' (paqad) means that God turns his attention to someone and acts on a promise.
rules_and_mechanics: God acts as he had said, so a promised birth becomes a fulfilment of his word.
The birth happens at the appointed time named in the promise.
The child receives a name tied to the promise or the joy it brings.

systems.name: Weaning feast
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Children were weaned at about two or three years old, so surviving to weaning was an occasion to celebrate a child's survival and standing in the household.
rules_and_mechanics: The head of the household holds the feast, a 'great' one for an heir.
It takes place on the day the child is weaned.
It marks the child's place in the family and, here, sharpens the question of who will inherit.

systems.name: Witness gift of lambs
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Where wells were scarce, disputes over water rights were settled by a witnessed act; a gift accepted before witnesses served as a proof of ownership or claim.
rules_and_mechanics: The claimant gives a gift of animals to the other party.
Accepting the gift means admitting the claimant dug the well.
A name or oath at the place commemorates the agreement.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham and Abimelech make a covenant at Beer-sheba, after which Abimelech and Phicol go back to the land of the Philistines.
system_instances.significance_note: It brings peace between Abraham and the Philistine king and secures Abraham's stay.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham plants a tamarisk at Beer-sheba and calls on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
system_instances.significance_note: The patriarch fixes his worship at Beer-sheba and names God as eternal, a title found only here.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God tells Abraham to do as Sarah says and promises to make Ishmael a nation too.
system_instances.significance_note: God confirms Isaac as the line of the promise while promising Ishmael a future, which resolves Abraham's distress.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The angel of God calls to Hagar from heaven; God has heard the boy, and she is shown a well.
system_instances.significance_note: God saves the outcast mother and son, and repeats the promise of a great nation, which echoes ch. 16.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham rises early, gives Hagar bread and a skin of water and sends her away with the boy.
system_instances.significance_note: The household splits in two: Isaac stays as sole heir and Ishmael leaves with his mother.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham circumcises Isaac when he is eight days old, as God commanded.
system_instances.significance_note: Abraham obeys the covenant command of ch. 17 for the covenant heir.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham calls his newborn son Isaac.
system_instances.significance_note: The name 'he laughs' carries the laughter of ch. 17 and ch. 18 and Sarah's joy in vv. 6–7.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham holds a great feast on the day Isaac is weaned.
system_instances.significance_note: The feast displays Isaac as the heir and sets the scene for Sarah's reaction to Ishmael.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham sets seven ewe lambs apart and Abimelech accepts them as witness that Abraham dug the well.
system_instances.significance_note: The gift gives the legal basis for Abraham's claim and for the name Beer-sheba.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The two men swear together at the place, which is called Beer-sheba.
system_instances.significance_note: The oath gives the place its name and a lasting memory of the agreement.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The LORD visits Sarah as he had said, and she conceives and bears a son at the appointed time.
system_instances.significance_note: The long-promised heir is born, which fulfils the covenant promise and ends Sarah's barrenness.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham reproves Abimelech about a well his servants seized; Abimelech says he knew nothing of it.
system_instances.significance_note: It shows water rights as a source of conflict and sets up the covenant that settles it.

edges.description: Abimelech asks Abraham to swear by God that he will not deal falsely with him or his descendants.
Abraham circumcises his son Isaac on the eighth day as God commanded.
Abraham gives Abimelech sheep and oxen and makes a covenant with him.
Abraham reproves Abimelech about a well that Abimelech's servants had seized.
Abraham gives Hagar bread and water and sends her away with the boy.
Abraham and Abimelech swear an oath to each other at the place later called Beer-sheba.
God hears the boy's voice where he lies and answers by calling to Hagar from heaven.
God opens Hagar's eyes so that she sees a well and can give the boy water.
God says he will make the son of the slave woman a nation because he is Abraham's offspring.
God tells Abraham to listen to Sarah's voice because Isaac carries the line of his offspring.
The LORD visits Sarah and does for her what he had promised.
Hagar takes a wife for Ishmael from the land of Egypt.
Sarah tells Abraham to drive out the slave woman and her son so that Ishmael will not inherit with Isaac.
